back_translation: Who is this coming from Edom, from Bozrah in deep-dyed red garments? Who is this in splendid apparel, striding forward in his great strength? "It is I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to save."
Why is your apparel red, and your garments like those of one who treads the winepress?

"I have trodden the winepress alone, and not a single man from the peoples was with me. I trod them in my anger and trampled them in my wrath; their lifeblood spattered my garments, and I stained all my apparel.
For the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redemption had come.
I looked, but there was no helper; I was appalled that there was no one to uphold. So my own arm brought me salvation, and my own wrath upheld me.
I trampled the peoples in my anger; I made them drunk with my wrath, and I poured their lifeblood down to the ground."

I will recount the steadfast love of the LORD and the praises of the LORD, according to all the LORD has done for us — the abundant goodness to the house of Israel, which he has granted them according to his compassion and the abundance of his steadfast love.
He said, "Surely they are my people, sons who will not betray." So he became their Savior.
In all their distress he too was distressed, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and his tender compassion he redeemed them; he lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.
But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit. So he turned and became their enemy, and he himself fought against them.
Then his people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses: Where is he who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where is he who set his Holy Spirit in their midst,
who made his glorious arm lead at Moses' right hand, who split the waters before them to make for himself an everlasting name,
who led them through the depths? They did not stumble — like a horse running in open country.
Like cattle going down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD gave them rest. Thus you led your people, to make for yourself a glorious name.
Look down from heaven and see, from your holy and glorious dwelling. Where are your zeal and your might? Your deep yearning and your compassion are withheld from us.
For you are our Father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us. You, O LORD, are our Father; your name is Our Redeemer from Everlasting.
O LORD, why do you let us wander from your ways and harden our hearts so that we do not fear you? Return, for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your inheritance.
Your holy people possessed it only a little while; then our adversaries trampled your sanctuary.
We have become like those you never ruled, like those never called by your name. Oh, that you would tear open the heavens and come down, so that the mountains would quake before your face!
